facts.heading: Anxiety worse since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it has gotten worse since September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Made deputy head at school
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school. She has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school. I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxious thoughts happen mostly on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing staff meeting
facts.content: Hannah rehearses possible questions and what she would say for staff meetings.
facts.evidence: I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head. Every possible question someone might ask, and what I'd say.

facts.heading: Fear of incompetence
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: No external feedback
facts.content: No one has said anything that suggests Hannah's fears are valid.
facts.evidence: No. That's the strange thing. Nobody has. It's all in my head.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr Hargreaves

facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling of inauthenticity

facts.evidence: I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah compares her current job to her mother's career.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother was a headteacher

facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy

facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother retired six years ago
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago

facts.heading: Mother's library named

facts.evidence: they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Hiding feelings from mother

facts.evidence: So I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Waking at four AM

facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term.

facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms

facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A child laughing, a good email.

facts.evidence: As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook.
